name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development due to 5-Alpha-Reductase 2 Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 5α-Reductase 2 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual
Elevated serum testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (T/DHT) ratio after hCG stimulation test
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the SRD5A2 gene by molecular genetic testing
Absence of Müllerian duct derivatives (uterus, fallopian tubes) confirmed by imaging
Positive family history of 46,XY DSD or consanguinity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY individual plus elevated T/DHT ratio and confirmation of SRD5A2 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by biochemical testing combined with molecular genetic analysis.

laboratory: Elevated serum testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (T/DHT) ratio (>10) after hCG stimulation
Normal or elevated baseline testosterone levels
Normal luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing absence of Müllerian structures
Testicular ultrasound to assess cryptorchidism or microlithiasis
other: Histopathology of testes may show normal Leydig and Sertoli cells
Clinical examination revealing ambiguous genitalia and hypospadias

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations
Absent or sparse pubic and axillary hair
Impaired conversion of androstenedione to testosterone
Low testosterone levels with ambiguous genitalia
Different enzyme defect confirmed by genetic testing

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia in a newborn 46,XY individual
Elevated testosterone to dihydrotestosterone ratio after hCG stimulation
Delayed or incomplete virilization during puberty
references: Maimoun L, Philibert P, Cammas B, et al. 5α-Reductase type 2 deficiency: Clinical and molecular aspects. Ann Endocrinol (Paris). 2011;72(2):91-96.
Imperato-McGinley J, Guerrero L, Gautier T, et al. Steroid 5α-reductase deficiency in man: An inherited form of male pseudohermaphroditism. Science. 1974;186(4170):1213-1215.
Hiort O. 5α-Reductase deficiency: Clinical features and molecular genetics. Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2002;198(1-2):51-59.
